name: LIFE Nature and Biodiversity: Standard Action Projects

administered_by.name: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)

summary: Annual EU call for nature conservation and restoration projects that help implement the Birds and Habitats Directives, manage the Natura 2000 network and protect species and habitats, open to public and private bodies established in the EU and LIFE-associated countries.

geography.label: EU Member States (including overseas countries and territories), listed EEA countries and countries associated to the LIFE Programme

reporting: Projects report outputs and impacts against the LIFE Project Indicators; longer projects may also submit progress reports, and a final report (with GIS data where relevant) closes the grant.

eligibility.rule: Target only wild flora, fauna, or natural and semi-natural habitats
Have stable, sufficient resources to implement the project and contribute the applicant share
Have the expertise, qualifications, resources, and relevant project experience
Inside Natura 2000, target only species and habitats listed in the site's official SDF
Outside Natura 2000, area-based actions must improve the network's ecological coherence
For reintroduction or translocation, have a documented prior agreement among all parties
Project does not cover recurring habitat management already under way before it starts
The proposed project has not already been completed

co_finance.applies_to: Priority-only projects; all other projects bring at least 40%

documents: Formal competent-authority letter for designation, update or adoption, if applicable
Competent-authority letter to update the Natura 2000 data sheet, if applicable
Commitment to legal protection status or long-term contractual agreement for outside-Natura activities, if applicable
Proof that purchased land price is not above the average, if applicable
Evidence that purchased land was not publicly owned in the previous 24 months, if applicable
Participant information, including previous projects if any

administered_by.quote: The European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA) presented the LIFE 2026 Calls for proposals during the EU LIFE 2026 info days.

applicant_types.quote: In order to be eligible, the applicants (beneficiaries and affiliated entities) must: - be legal entities (public or private bodies)

geography.quote: EU Member States (including overseas countries and territories (OCTs)) - non-EU countries: - listed EEA countries and countries associated to the LIFE Programme

access.quote: Proposals can only be submitted electronically through the Funding & Tenders portal.

window.quote: On 21 April, the European Commission launched the LIFE Programme Calls for proposals 2026.

co_finance_required.quote: Grant applications must ensure a balanced project budget and sufficient other resources to implement the project successfully (e.g. own contributions, income generated by the action, financial contributions from third parties, etc).

consortium_required.quote: In mono-beneficiary grants, the single beneficiary will automatically be coordinator.

reporting.quote: All LIFE proposals will have to report on their expected outputs and impacts taking into account the LIFE Project Indicators (LPIs).

eligibility.quote: Only wild flora and fauna and natural and semi-natural habitats may be targeted.
Applicants must have stable and sufficient resources to successfully implement the projects and contribute their share.

Applicants must have the know-how, qualifications and resources to successfully implement the projects and contribute their share (including sufficient experience in projects of comparable size and nature).
Activities can only target species and habitats listed in the site's official Natura 2000 Standard Data Form (SDF).
are allowed outside Natura 2000 only for the improvement of the ecological coherence/connectivity of the Natura 2000 network to build a coherent Trans-European Nature Network.

a prior agreement between all parties involved (e.g. between the competent authority for the donor population and the manager of the area of reintroduction or introduction/translocation) has been concluded and documented;
Annual or otherwise recurring habitat management actions that were already ongoing before the start of the project are not eligible.
Proposals for projects that have already been completed will be rejected;

co_finance.quote: The costs will be reimbursed at the funding rate fixed in the Grant Agreement (maximum 60%). You can apply for a higher project funding rate if your project is a 'project targeting exclusively priority habitats/species' (75%)

documents.quote: detailed cost breakdown in the 'detailed budget table' mandatory annex.
submit a formal letter from the MS competent authority committing to the designation/formal update/adoption before the end of the project;
a letter of commitment from the competent authority to update the data sheet before the end of the project
in the form of a commitment for giving these sites the most appropriate legal protection status or long-term contractual agreement before the end of the project.
proof that the price per hectare is not above the average for the types of land and locations concerned, must be provided with the proposal
Evidence must be provided that the land purchased was not owned by a public authority in the 24 months prior to the project application date.
participant information (including previous projects, if any).

effort.quote: The proposals will have to follow the standard submission and evaluation procedure (one-stage submission + one-step evaluation).

after_award.quote: There will be one or more additional prefinancing payments linked to a prefinancing report.

If relevant, projects must upload a Geographic Information System (GIS) file and associated data of the specific geographical area where the intervention took place as a deliverable in their final report.

steps: Full proposal via the Funding & Tenders Portal
